source_meta._title: Item frames/Glow item frames don't change their hitbox if they contain a map

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition client running the exact affected build Minecraft 1.7.1; fresh single-player Creative mode world; keyboard and mouse controls, with Attack/Destroy and Use Item mapped to known inputs. No dedicated server or second player is required.
preconditions: Use a disposable world created directly in Minecraft 1.7.1; do not open an important newer-version world in this historical build.
Create the test world in Creative mode so the required blocks and items can be obtained deterministically without crafting or commands.
Leave at least one hotbar slot empty for the trigger action.
Use a regular Item Frame in the recommended version. Glow Item Frames do not exist in Minecraft 1.7.1, so the glow variant requires a later listed affected version.
Perform the test against a vertical wall made from ordinary solid full blocks; this plan uses Stone as a deterministic practical choice.

The instructions refer to the default controls E for inventory, right-click for Use Item/Place Block, left-click for Attack/Destroy, and F3+B for entity hitboxes. If controls are rebound, use the bindings assigned to those actions.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using an installation configured for the exact build named "Minecraft 1.7.1" in the report. If the launcher hides historical builds, enable its option to display historical Java Edition versions before selecting the build.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running game version as 1.7.1.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set the game mode to Creative, and create the world. The world name and seed may be arbitrary because the report supplies neither and no generated structure is required.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new Creative mode world.

steps.action: Wait before building until the terrain immediately around the player has rendered and movement responds normally. Move to a nearby open, level area with enough room to stand several blocks in front of a wall.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, player movement is responsive, and there is clear space for a three-block-wide wall and a viewing position in front of it.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab, represented by a compass icon, to locate Stone, Item Frame, and Empty Map. Move at least nine Stone blocks, one Item Frame, and one Empty Map into separate hotbar slots. Keep one other hotbar slot empty, then press E again to close the inventory.
steps.exact_input: E; search terms: stone, item frame, empty map
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains Stone, an Item Frame, and an Empty Map in separate slots, and at least one hotbar slot remains empty.

steps.action: Select Stone using its hotbar number key. On level ground, place Stone blocks with right-click to construct a vertical wall three blocks wide and three blocks tall. Keep the front face unobstructed and identify the block in the exact center of the wall as the support block for the item frame.
steps.success_cue: A solid 3-by-3 vertical Stone wall is present, with enough clear space to stand directly in front of its center block.

steps.action: Select the Empty Map in the hotbar. While standing in the world with no inventory screen open, press right-click once to use the Empty Map and convert it into a filled map.
steps.success_cue: The selected item is now a filled map and displays mapped terrain when held.

steps.action: Select the Item Frame in the hotbar. Face the front of the 3-by-3 wall, aim the crosshair at the exposed vertical face of the wall's center Stone block, and right-click once to attach the Item Frame.
steps.success_cue: One regular Item Frame is attached to the front face of the center Stone block.

steps.action: Select the filled map in the hotbar. Aim the crosshair at the center of the attached Item Frame and right-click once to insert the map into it.
steps.success_cue: The filled map is displayed in the Item Frame and its visible map surface covers the face of the center wall block.

steps.action: Press the number key corresponding to the deliberately empty hotbar slot. Do not hold Stone, another block, or an item that performs a secondary action during the trigger.
steps.exact_input: Number key for an empty hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The active hotbar slot is empty while the filled map remains in the Item Frame.

steps.action: Hold F3 and press B once to enable the entity-hitbox overlay. On keyboards where function keys control hardware features, also hold Fn if required. F3+B was available before the recommended version and can be used to make the Item Frame's target boundary visible. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.4.4/Development_versions?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The entity-hitbox overlay is enabled and an outline is visible around the Item Frame entity.

steps.action: Stand approximately two to three blocks directly in front of the framed map and face it squarely. Adjust the camera until the entire map surface, the support block face, and the Item Frame hitbox outline are easy to distinguish. Do not click either mouse button yet.
steps.exact_input: Mouse movement; movement keys as needed
steps.success_cue: The full map is in view from the front, the hitbox outline is visible, and no interaction has yet been performed at an outer edge or corner.

steps.action: Move the crosshair to one outer corner region of the visible map. Place it between the visible map boundary and the nearest edge of the Item Frame's hitbox outline: the crosshair must be outside the outlined Item Frame hitbox, but still slightly inside the map graphic and inside the face of the center Stone support block. Do not aim exactly on the seam between wall blocks.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair rests over a visible outer corner region of the map, outside the Item Frame hitbox outline but within the center support block's face.

steps.action: Without moving the crosshair, press and release the left mouse button exactly once to perform one Attack/Destroy interaction at that outer map corner. Do not hold the button and do not repeat the interaction.
steps.success_cue: One attack input has just been issued at the outer map corner, and no additional input has been made.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just left-clicked once on a visible outer corner of the filled map while the crosshair was outside the Item Frame's displayed hitbox outline but inside the face of its Stone support block. Stop all further input and begin observing which object received the interaction.
uncertainties: The report provides no world seed, coordinates, required game mode, or wall material. A fresh Creative single-player world and a 3-by-3 Stone wall are practical choices that minimize unrelated crafting, exploration, and survival requirements.

The report lists Minecraft 1.7.1 first, so it is the required recommended version even though it is a historical pre-release build. Its exact availability or label may depend on the launcher installation interface.

Glow Item Frames were added in snapshot 21w03a and therefore cannot be tested in the recommended Minecraft 1.7.1 build. This plan tests the regular Item Frame variant described by the original report; a separate glow-frame run would need to use 21w03a or another later affected version that contains Glow Item Frames. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Barang?utm_source=openai))

The report says to interact "in any way" at a corner or edge. This plan selects one left-click Attack/Destroy input because it is a single, deterministic trigger that directly tests whether the corner targets the framed-map entity or its support block.

The F3+B overlay is used only to make corner targeting repeatable. The report does not explicitly require the overlay as a reproduction precondition, although a report comment mentions F3+B and external version-history information confirms that the shortcut predates Minecraft 1.7.1. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.4.4/Development_versions?utm_source=openai))
